name: Galantine of Veal
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: A little cooked ham or tongue
ingredients.originalText: A little cooked ham or tongue
ingredients.quantityText: A little cooked ham or tongue

instructions.text: Mix with the sausage meat the breadcrumbs, nutmeg, salt, and pepper
Put half in the veal, then some ham cut in long strips, then walnuts, then more sausage meat, then ham and walnuts
Tuck the veal over it and sew up
Tie up in a cloth very firmly at ends and stitch cloth at top
Put into boiling water and boil for two and a half hours
After it is boiled put between two boards to press
Brush the veal over with glaze made from half ounce gelatine, one cup of stock, and a drop of carmine two or three times

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Mix with the sausage meat the breadcrumbs, nutmeg, salt, and pepper
2. Put half in the veal, then some ham cut in long strips, then walnuts, then more sausage meat, then ham and walnuts
3. Tuck the veal over it and sew up
4. Tie up in a cloth very firmly at ends and stitch cloth at top
5. Put into boiling water and boil for two and a half hours
6. After it is boiled put between two boards to press
7. Brush the veal over with glaze made from half ounce gelatine, one cup of stock, and a drop of carmine two or three times
